traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 371 Marantaceae: perennial herbs; leaves in two ranks, with an open sheath, a stalk thickened as a hinge below the blade, and a blade with many close parallel veins running obliquely from the midrib; flowers bisexual, lopsided, in a bracted spike or panicle; perianth mostly of calyx and corolla, the inner three unequal; one fertile stamen with a one-celled anther, the rest petal-like staminodes; ovary inferior, of 3 to 1 cells; fruit fleshy or a capsule.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Marantaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
